files.title: Runox
files.body: **Runox** — Known as the Crimson Harborer, Runox is a hateful, revenge-driven Luxian man standing around six feet tall with dark curly hair resembling a modern mullet, whose entire existence has been shaped by rejection and a profound inability to belong anywhere. Born in the The Luxian Empire, he was deemed a defective child by the holy prophets and discarded — tossed off the island and left to whatever fate All Father would decide for him. He survived, landing in a giant moss quarry in the The Virethorian Empire where he was discovered and raised by two Virethorian artisans who gave him a normal upbringing, yet Runox could never truly fit in. His Luxian physiology made him visibly different, and the constant belittling from those around him made him feel like neither a true Luxian nor a true Virethorian — he had the gifted body of a Luxian but couldn't live up to their high standards, and the isolationist culture of the Virethorian Empire kept him trapped and ignorant of his own origins. This identity crisis cultivated a deep-seated hatred and a singular obsession with combat as an outlet, with Runox ultimately caring about nothing more than the thrill of the fight and the pursuit of revenge against a world that discarded him. In battle, he wields the Orbs of Crimson as his Power Core, condensing crimson energy into tiny, incredibly dense and destructive balls that he uses in versatile and adaptive ways — firing them like bullets from his fingertip in a finger gun motion for ranged combat, or crushing them in his palm to coat his hand in raw crimson for devastating close-quarters strikes. Uniquely, wherever Runox bleeds, he can generate a new crimson orb, making him more dangerous the longer a fight goes on. He is also capable of |Hyperdash III and can occasionally push into |Hyperdash IV , making him a highly mobile and unpredictable fighter who adapts his crimson abilities to whatever the situation demands.

files.title: All Father
files.body: **All Father** — Simply known as God, All Father is an eternal, deity-level being of unknown race who resides in the The Cradle Above and stands as the single most powerful entity in the world of Baroque, worshipped as a religious figure and holding ultimate authority over the distribution of Power Cores — deciding who receives them and who doesn't, though his motivation for this is rooted not in benevolence but in his own insatiable hunger, as he ultimately devours Power Cores to feed an eternal craving that can never truly be satisfied. His appearance is unlike anything mortal — an all-white humanoid entity that radiates a blinding, intense glow resembling a pure white sun, with black flaring eyes and the well-built silhouette of a powerful man, emanating an aura of unwavering, relentless, and overwhelming power so intense that his mere presence alone is reported to render people unconscious. This is fitting, as encounters with All Father are exceptionally rare — most who have seen him have not survived. He wields no Power Core of his own, instead surpassing every known limit of strength, speed, and endurance so completely that the concept of a Power Core is beneath him. His primary combat ability involves making devastating cuts and slashes at any location he chooses simply by waving or swiping his arm — these cuts can range from a light scratch to splitting a target completely in half, and he can execute them at will with virtually no energy expenditure. His fighting style is one of supreme, casual indifference — he walks, stands his ground, and allows outside forces to throw him around without concern, cutting down anything and anyone at his leisure, nearly invincible and entirely unbothered, a being for whom combat is not a challenge but simply an extension of existing.

files.title: Chariot
files.body: **Chariot** — Known as the Blind Magician, Chariot is a |Nivoran warrior and one of the most powerful and feared members of the The Glacier Force, a ruthless fighter whose cold exterior and devastating combat ability were forged entirely from tragedy, grief, and manipulation. He dresses in black, grey, and dark red cloth robes resembling a trench coat, wears a black blindfold over his sightless eyes, and carries himself with a permanently cold and stern expression that reflects a life hardened far beyond its years. Chariot grew up in a cabin on the outskirts of Nivora with his mother, deeply admiring the Glacier Force — of which his father was a leading figure — and would even defend the organization against villagers who spoke out against them. That admiration was shattered on the night a Snowbiter Hunt went undetected by the scouting team, resulting in a surprise attack that decimated his village, broke into his home, massacred his mother, and cost Chariot his eyes. The overwhelming trauma and grief of that moment triggered the awakening of his Power Core, Man of Myth, which he unleashed to annihilate the entire pack of Snowbiters. In the aftermath, the emotionally shattered and vulnerable Chariot was taken in by the Glacier Force elders, who recognized the raw power of his ability and deliberately exploited his unstable state to mold him into a weapon for their own agenda — something Chariot would only come to understand much later. Despite his blindness, Chariot is a formidable physical combatant thanks to his sharpened hearing, wielding a long staff in close coordination with his summoned entity in a tight, disciplined fighting style where he keeps himself and his entity in close proximity, operating almost like a two-person unit. He extends his entity outward only when the situation calls for it, and is capable of Hyperdash II.

files.title: Emperor Blitz
files.body: **Emperor Blitz** — Known as the Thunder Berserker, Emperor Blitz is a Luxian emperor, a member of the The Luxian Elite Force and one of the most physically imposing and authoritative figures in the world, commanding a heavy, suffocating presence that reflects his iron-fisted rule over his empire. He is an enormously bulky and robust figure, almost always encased in massive black metal-plated berserker armor lined with heavy insulated padding designed to retain heat, with reinforced metal plates on his palms specifically engineered for his signature combat technique. Unlike many fighters who develop their abilities by circumstance or hardship, Blitz grew up in royalty and forged himself through discipline — training relentlessly as a teenager to master his powers before entering military service as a young adult, where he proved to be a ruthless and devastating general capable of single-handedly decimating entire populations. His Power Core Ability, Han-Zen, gives him mastery over lightning, which he channels primarily through his palm strikes — driving his armored palm into a victim and then surging concentrated electricity through them, either stunning them in place or burning their skin if sustained. He can escalate this further into a massive thunder-strike, overloading the opponent with electricity and sending them flying. Defensively, his armor-clad strategy is brilliantly passive — he lets enemies strike his metal plating and uses Han-Zen to channel their impact back as an electric shock. On the rare occasions he removes his armor entirely, he sacrifices his defensive bulk in exchange for tremendous speed and the ability to use HyperdashIII, and in select cases HyperdashIV, transforming from an immovable fortress into a terrifyingly fast and lethal combatant.

files.description: The Hyper dash is essentially a super dash that can be broken down into four tiers. It is typically used by users to close distances or make distance as quickly…
files.body: ## Hyper-dash The Hyper dash is essentially a super dash that can be broken down into four tiers. It is typically used by users to close distances or make distance as quickly as possible. It is a fundamental skill that most fighters train to learn. #### Hyper Dash I: The most basic form. Involves a quick velocity burst, covering mediocre distance and leaving a tiny dust trail behind the user. It is pretty slow, like a normal human dash. #### Hyper Dash II: Still basic but a slightly better form. It also involves a quick velocity burst and can travel a LOT farther than Hyper Dash I. It usually cracks the ground where the user left, leaving a huge smoke trail. This is harnessed by a well trained fighter. #### Hyper Dash III: Much more advances than any of the predecessors and it is often used by very advanced fighters. The dash is almost instantaneous and devastatingly destroys the ground where the user left, leaving a giant sonic boom and dust. It can cover massive distances. #### Hyper Dash IV: The strongest form, often wielded by the strongest or a super charged state. The dash is instantaneous and can travel ridiculously far, leaving a giant sonic boom, destroying all the ground behind the user as the user dashes, leaving a trail of dust and rubble.

files.title: Tarkan
files.body: **Tarkan** — Classified as a Medium Threat and belonging to the reptile species, the Tarkan are large, pterodactyl-like flying creatures native exclusively to the Plagued Zone, their dark brown bodies streaked with green mossy lines and cracks that reflect their deep biological integration with the corrupted, toxic environment they call home — different breeds display varying patterns and color combinations, but all share the same long slender wings and beefy, powerful build. The Tarkan are so thoroughly adapted to the Plagued Zone's toxic atmosphere that they breathe it fluently and naturally, but this adaptation comes at a serious cost: when removed from the plagued air of their home region, Tarkans struggle to breathe, making them creatures that are fundamentally tethered to the corrupted environment that shaped them. They are herbivores, feeding off the plagued plants of their home zone, and in terms of temperament they are naturally passive and pack-oriented — content to live alongside their own kind without aggression unless provoked, at which point they become highly dangerous. Their intelligence sits roughly at the level of a horse, but notably, Tarkans possess the ability to understand emotion, which likely plays a significant role in how The Virethorian Empire has managed to tame and work with them so effectively. The Virethorians have elevated Tarkan domestication into a sophisticated military and transportation technology — carefully engineering jet engines, saddles, weapons mounts, and breathing apparatus directly onto the creatures, merging living biology with mechanical engineering to create the Tarkan Jet, a hybrid aerial vehicle that serves the empire in battle, transport, and as a weapons platform, representing one of the most unique and formidable military assets in all of Baroque.

files.title: Zippercadia
files.body: **Zippercadia** — Classified as a Low Threat and belonging to the bug species, the Zippercadia are small, dragonfly-like insects native to the colder areas of the Sky Islands, where they exist in large and abundant swarms, zipping through the air with the erratic, rapid movement of water skippers but airborne, their dark blue bodies traced with light blue lines and encased in relatively hard shells that protect them from the environment. What makes the Zippercadia far more remarkable than their small size suggests is their innate ability to conduct and chain electricity between one another — when two or more Zippercadia are in proximity, they naturally form living electrical connections, and when enough of them gather together, the combined electrical output of their chained network becomes genuinely devastating, transforming a swarm of tiny insects into a cascading web of lethal voltage. They are completely immune to electricity and shocks themselves, which is what allows them to sustain and channel these connections without harm. In terms of behavior, the Zippercadia are naturally evasive and conflict-averse, preferring to avoid other living things unless forced into contact, and they sleep while airborne inside clouds to stay hidden and protected — a clever survival adaptation that, combined with their incredible speed, makes them extremely difficult to catch under normal circumstances. Their diet is simple, consisting of other bugs and seeds, and their intelligence is average — just enough to know how to survive. Despite their evasiveness, The Luxian Empire has developed a brutal and highly effective method of weaponizing them: Zippercadia are captured in large quantities and frozen to the precise threshold where they remain alive but completely paralyzed, then mounted onto arrows fired by thousands of Luxian troops simultaneously, creating a massive, sky-spanning conducting chain of arrows that delivers an enormous coordinated electrical strike — turning the empire's most abundant local insect into one of its most fearsome military assets.

files.title: Snowbiters
files.body: **Snowbiters** — Classified as Feral and Hazardous, the Snowbiters are among the most terrifying and relentless mammals in all of Baroque, serving as the dominant apex predators of the Sub-zero Summits and the single greatest ongoing threat to the people of Nivora, whose entire military culture and way of life has been shaped around the constant pressure these creatures apply. Physically, the Snowbiter is a massive, wolf-like, saber-toothed four-legged beast covered in thick coats of white and grey fur that have, on most individuals, taken on patches of deep red from the sheer accumulated volume of blood soaked into them over a lifetime of hunting — their canine teeth are long, sharp, and perpetually stained with dried blood and gore, and nearly every Snowbiter carries visible scarring from a life of relentless, fearless combat. What makes the Snowbiter particularly dangerous is not just its raw physicality but its intelligence — the creature operates at a cognitive level nearly equal to a human, allowing it to form organized hunting packs, build and maintain igloo communities where they rest between hunts, and coordinate attacks with a level of strategic awareness that makes them far more than simple animals. They make no gender distinctions within their social structure and show absolute loyalty to their own pack while dominating everything else around them with zero sense of self-preservation or fear — a Snowbiter will take on any opponent regardless of size or threat, making them as psychologically terrifying as they are physically deadly. Their diet consists entirely of the flesh of any living creature, and they supplement their water intake by chewing ice directly, meaning the frozen wasteland of the Sub-zero Summits provides them with everything they need to thrive. Their primary weakness is heat, which can overwhelm them quickly given their adaptation to extreme cold, and while the theoretical potential for taming exists — they can be drawn by flesh and blood — their high intelligence makes them extremely difficult to exploit or control in practice.

files.title: Power Core System
files.description: All Father is a divine entity that sits outside of the observable reality, above all realms.
files.body: ### All Father - God Himself All Father is a divine entity that sits outside of the observable reality, above all realms. All Father represents an absolute peak in power for he is all powerful and divine. He resides in the The Cradle Above, a literal and metaphorical place above all. #### Personality and Behavior: All Father is neither good or bad, he is simply hungry. He needs to feast on Power Cores to keep his body working, LOTS of them. He simply sits in the Cradle Above and feasts until it comes time to rest. During that rest period, the Power Cores that pass remain uneaten. All Father also comes down to the observable reality to deal with crisis that threatens his position. All Father seeks only to eat, he is eternally hungry and that's his only incentive. His hunger however, dictates the fate of many in the observable reality ### The Cradle Above The Cradle Above, a liminal, white and misty metaphorical and literal place and All Father's domain, holds streams. Streams are metaphysical rivers that hold different components that form the human. Said components float on the river, taking a tangible form and the river leads to a waterfall at the end of the Cradle Above. These components then fall into their respective human once they reach the waterfall exit. A component enters the stream as a human is conceived. There exists a mind stream (which drops personality orbs into its respective human), a soul stream (which drops the metaphysical soul into its respective human) and a Power Core stream (which is responsible for dropping power cores into humans). For example, once a human is conceived, a mind component, soul component and power core component is formed and dropped into the river. These components then follow the river until they get to the edge of the Cradle Above and fall off the water fall, falling into the human that was conceived. All Father stays near the Power Core stream and feasts on them until it comes time to rest. Any human that is born during this brief rest period gets a Power Core since when All Father isn't resting, they are being eaten. ### The Power Core The Power Core is like the soul in many ways but its also like an organ. It is a soul-organ hybrid. The Power Core resembles a spherical, glassy energy ball in the Power Core Stream. The Power Core holds a very specific ability (with an equal cost) that would go to the person it was meant for. All Father feasts on them and the ones that get past him during his rest land in their respective human and they gain the Power Core as a pseudo-organ. Once obtained, the organ needs to be activated given a criteria. It is important to remember each power comes with a cost. There are many ways to recognize a power core ability. Firstly, Ignition Moment's are the main activation criteria. Another way to figure out what one's power core ability is readings done by Power Core Shaman. They can tap into the soul and read a Power Core ability, #### Core Law (Immutable Power): - Once conceived and embedded, a power core cannot be changed, evolved, upgraded, fractured, or reshaped. - Each chosen person receives exactly one power core, containing exactly one style of power — no hybrids, no changes over time. - Core abilities do not scale with emotion or growth. Instead, mastery comes from spiritual discipline and understanding one's inherent limits. #### Classifications: Power Core's have a few basic classifications ###### Enhancer: Power Core abilities of enhancers involve powers that enhance the physical body ###### Conceiver: Power Core abilities of conceivers involve bringing forth something into reality ###### Manipulator: Power Core abilities of manipulators involve manipulating already existent matter or imbuing matter with something ##### Harnesser: Power Core abilities of harnessers involve harnessing energy or some essence already found in reality #### Activation Criteria: Powers are dormant until a natural point during adolescence, typically triggered by intense emotional/spiritual stress. This is known as an **Ignition Moment** #### Transference: It is possible to transfer someone else's Power Core into another. This can be done intentionally via Spiritual Surgeries where it is transferred like an organ. To even see the Power Core and work with it, a spiritual entanglement between the two parties must happen. This can be done in many ways: Rituals, Emotional Connections, etc.. ###### Core Theft: It is possible to steal a Power Core like an organ. Firstly, to even see or access the tangible core, a spiritual entanglement between the thief and the victim must commence, often through some sort of ritual. It is important to note that Power Core's are very unique to its user so a lot of the time, someone else's Power Core would be dangerous to the thief. Sometimes however, when the two individuals are very spiritually and mentally similar, the Power Core is compatible ###### Ritual Examples: - **The Rite of Hollowing** – Involves separating one’s soul from the body to implant a core. - **Soul Chamber Binding** – Requires the thief and victim to be spiritually entangled, often through bloodline or emotional connection. - **God’s Mirror** – A mythical artifact said to reflect and reverse a soul imprint — possibly used in core swapping. ### Summary: Essentially the Power Core is an organ like component that every human is meant to have upon conception. The Power Core gets inserted into the human by following the stream in The Cradle Above and falling off the waterfall into the body of it's human. Every human however, does not receive his or her Power Core because All Father feasts on them as they come on the stream. Once All Father has his rest however, the Power Cores can freely fall into their human and this is why very few individuals have a Power Core and even fewer activate it. Once activated, the Power Core grants the user with a power following one of the classifications above and this power follows the Core Law. Each Power comes with a cost.

files.title: (3)Zorak'S Wrath
files.description: Vivaan Kaushal
files.body: Vivaan Kaushal 7/22/25 1940 --- "ZO-RAK! ZO-RAK! ZO-RAK!" The crowd chants in such perfect synchronization, thousands of voices folded down into one. They collectively follow up by synchronously stomping their feet; STOMP STOMP — STOMP STOMP — STOMP STOMP. Dust lifts off the floor of the ring and hangs there, refusing to settle. The crowd, barbaric at heart but civil at glance, men and women alike, go crazy. A large, old, giant, wooden door with rusty medieval metal lining gets pulled up by a near pristine condition rope within one of the walls of the Gladiator Ring. It groans the whole way. Out walks a man. "ZO-RAK! ZO-RAK! ZO-RAK!" The symphony of stomps shook the ring. In the middle of the ring are five shirtless men in underwear. They all seem relatively fit and healthy. Gleaming skin, toned muscles, a skeptical look. They look forward, glancing at the man walking out. Some look with confidence, and some shattered with fear. As he enters the warm hug of the sun, his left arm glistens. He performs slow arm circles with it, and the whole limb catches the light in one solid sheet — a pristine, threatening metal alloy, joint plates sliding over each other like something alive. This man is so youthful. He has such a confident look in his eyes. His eyes are that of a predator and they are locked at the five other men. He continues approaching. The sun reflects off his bald head and his medieval gladiator armor shines through the ring. The armor appears to be really light weight, more decoration than defense. On his back and belt are an assortment of weapons; spears, knives, maces and swords. He unbuckles all of it in one motion and throws it down in the sand in front of the five opposing men. The pile clatters and settles. "Choose your weapons wisely." He glances at all five men. He makes sure to lock eyes with each man for exactly two seconds, no more, no less. His eyes speak nothing but pure admiration and respect. The five men choose their weapons. Two men pick knives. One picks a spear. One man dual wields two short maces. The last man, taller than the rest and far too calm for a man about to die, waits until the pile is picked over before he takes the sword. The bald man takes off his heavy shoulder plates and throws them to the ground. He turns his back to the five men and looks up at the crowd whilst raising his hands with pure explosiveness. The show will commence. "ARRGHHHHHHHHHH!!!!" He yells with pure barbaric intent. The crowd goes wild. More stomps, more screams. People begin throwing shirts, flowers and other trinkets down into the ring. They rain into the sand around him. The gladiator ring shakes with passion. The bald man turns around to the men with nothing but an over the top smile. His teeth are out and about. He is insane, a complete psychopath. The opposing men now seem to be petrified in fear. One man? Versus the five of them? Their faces quickly turned confident after pondering this fact. --- High above the sand, behind stone rails and shaded silk, the box of the King sits full of the realm's elite. "Draven Zorak . . . The next heir to the throne . . . show us why you will bring us to further glory," The King says with pride in a room filled with many elite spectators. "Why would the heir participate in such games?" A rich spectator asks. "This gladiator match was arranged purely on Zorak's request. He's a hungry man indeed," The king boasts. "He does it for the love of the game. Honorable, yet hungry." --- Zorak kneels to the five men. "You men all deserve nothing but an eternal life with All Father. I wish you the best in the afterlife and utmost luck!" Zorak then proceeds to put the most heinous smile on his face. He rises and walks closer to the five opposing men. "Bring out your indomitable spirit, young men. Bring it forth." "How do you think we should approach this?" one opposing man says, the one with two maces. His grip keeps readjusting. "It's five against one. We should back up now to see his gameplan, and when we see a vulnerable opportunity we all collectively pounce on him," a man with a knife says. "He cannot block all of us at once, especially when our attack is a counter attack." The men continue to back up step by step as Zorak approaches. "Oh come on guys, let's put on a SHOW!" Within a blink of an eye, Zorak dashes right in front of the man in the middle, leaving a trail of dust behind him. The sand he stood in a moment ago collapses into the empty print of his foot. Zorak goes for an explosive left hook with his metal arm and the man reacts just at the nick of time, dodging it by leaning back. Upon missing, a giant burst of air blasts in the trajectory of his hook punch, leaving a giant wind shockwave that ripples the sand into a long, curved scar. "Was that due to his PUNCH??!!" the man with the sword says. They all jump back except the man who just dodged. "I DIDNT EVEN SEE HIM RUN, THIS SPEED!" Zorak follows up with an uppercut, aimed at the same man as before, only to be blasted back into the gladiator walls by a giant purple ghost whip. It comes out of nowhere, a long violet ribbon of light that cracks the air like a splitting mast. Zorak's impact leaves a huge crack on the peach, sandstone walls, and a fine rain of grit falls over the front row. The whip recoils and drinks itself back into the tall man's forearm. His sword lies forgotten in the sand behind him. Purple light braids up his elbow, humming, waiting. Zorak smirks. "A power core ability? HOW EXCITING!!" "Draven has no power core ability what so ever," The king explains to a spectator. "He relies on his training, skills and senses." Zorak stretches his back, rolling the metal shoulder until the plates click. "Let's deal with you first." He takes off, leaving an immense shockwave behind him, cracking the wall and ground further. He appears at the face of the power core wielder in mere milliseconds. The whip is already moving. It comes down in a screaming violet arc and Zorak crosses his metal arm over his head to eat it. The light wraps the alloy twice, tightens, and yanks — and for the first time all afternoon, Draven Zorak's feet leave the ground when he did not ask them to. "QUICK SURROUND HIM!" The four others come in from every angle to buy their champion the space he needs. As the men quickly get into position, Zorak tears free of the whip and spin hook kicks one of them, mangling and decapitating his head clean off. The maces drop first. His body collapses after, still standing for a half second on legs that don't know yet. One man goes in with the spear. Zorak leans in and weaves to the left, slimly avoiding the point whilst closing the distance. He then grabs the shaft and pulls the man in, elbowing him in the face with his metal arm. The impact releases a loud thump and crack sound as the man's jaw gets dislodged. It hangs like a dangling wire. Zorak follows up with a sweep, and as the man falls downwards, Zorak smashes his head in with one punch, splattering his skull on the sandy floor. The floor beneath cracks in a ring around his fist. The remaining two knifemen jump back but Zorak has already closed the distance in an instant. They go into complete adrenaline mode. Zorak throws the most nasty hook punch ever. The hook lands into the side of one of the men's heads and it sinks in. The metal arm crushes right through the skull and the head inevitably gives up and ends up exploding into a gory mess. The hook punch is so strong that the shockwave blasts some of the audience back and completely obliterates and cracks the floor all the way up to the wall. The last knifeman throws a couple of slash combos. Zorak blocks them with his metal arm with incredible precision, steel ringing on steel, sparks skipping off into the dust. He eventually catches his hand and rips it right off. Still being held by Zorak on the arm, the man is disarmed and throws another punch with his other hand. Zorak moves his head to the side and grabs the arm. He quickly turns around, flips the man over on his back and slams him into the floor. He then cracks his arm and kicks him so hard that he goes flying towards the wall. Zorak dashes in front of him mid-flight, grabs his neck and jumps upward with him, leaving a devastating crater beneath. He holds the man mid air and hurls him straight to the ground, splattering his body. His speed is inhumane. There is only one man left. --- Upon landing, Zorak gets right in his face as usual. Zorak throws some extremely powerful combos but the man dodges them. Head movement, small steps, nothing wasted. He ducks a hook and counter hooks Zorak's liver. Zorak actually feels that. "Whats up with this guy," Zorak thinks to himself. The man looks up with a smile on his face and headbutts Zorak so that he goes flying backwards. He then crashes into the ground. The man follows up and chases Zorak down. The whip snaps out of his arm again and lashes around Zorak's ankle, and he uses it like a rope — running with him, sliding him through the rough ground, carving a trench across the ring. He then whips him forward and Zorak crashes into the wall again. "That man, he is one of The Luxian Empire's finest gauntlet champions," The King explains. "We got him here a while ago. He's the one with the Ghost Whip power core ability" Zorak gets up out of the rubble, puzzled, but thrilled nonetheless. "I'll show you what strength is." Zorak blasts forward, rapidly approaching the Luxian man. He dashes all around him, throwing various attacks from every side at once. The Luxian man cannot keep up. He braces. Then he plants his feet and spins, sweeping the purple ghost whip in one enormous circle around his own body, a purple ring of light at knee height, and Zorak runs straight into it mid-dash. It takes his legs out from under him at full speed. He rolls, comes up, and throws a punch which the Luxian just barely avoids. He avoids it by pivoting to the side, leaving Zorak's arm trailing forward in front of his face. The Luxian then grabs Zorak's arm and uses the momentum to spin him, then slam him into the ground. Zorak round kicks the Luxian in the head from the ground, which he blocks, but he still gets knocked back. Zorak gets up and the two engage in long, precise and intense hand to hand combat. Punches and kicks fly back and forth. Dodges and weaves. Blocks and SPEED. They move around the ring, in and out of the shadow of the wall, sand exploding at every pivot. The audience goes silent. No longer yelling Zorak's name, they are extremely focused. Somewhere in the stands a single flower falls onto the sand and nobody watches it land. The Luxian throws two consecutive hook punches which Zorak ducks under, and drives his arms into the Luxian by his belly, driving him forward into a wall. The man hits the wall hard. Zorak looks up and lets go. He throws a punch with his metal arm. The Luxian moves his head to the left and the punch hits the wall, completely obliterating it, making a giant hole through the entire arena. Sunlight pours through the breach in a solid bar. It was like a giant bomb exploded at the wall. Many spectators got injured. With Zorak's arm still buried in the stone, the whip flares one last time and coils around his throat, hauling him backwards out of the hole. Zorak's metal hand comes up and catches the light itself. It hisses against the alloy. It does not break. The Luxian throws a swift back fist and Zorak catches that too. He quickly reacts by chopping the Luxian's face, leaving him a bit dazed. The purple light along his arm sputters, thins, gathers itself for another lash — and takes just a half beat too long doing it. At this very moment Zorak had sensed his opening. Zorak smiles and throws him across the arena, chasing him down right after he crashes into another wall. Zorak throws five consecutive punches one after another with his metal arm to the Luxian's face. Each punch blows a chunk of his face off, blood splurting everywhere. Zorak hook punches him, loosening his jaw. The Luxian attempts a swift combo and Zorak dodges all attacks. He then uppercut elbows the Luxian and rips his jaw off. He takes this jaw and slams it right into the Luxian's skull. The purple light goes out. "You fought well." He then drops the body and walks to the center of the ring. --- The audience goes wild once again, cheering his name. Zorak then proceeds to take off what appears to be leg weights, body weights and arm weights from his body. He unclasps them casually, the way a man takes off a coat. Upon dropping them to the ground, a DEVASTATING explosion ensues, turning the ground to rubble. The shock rolls up through the stone benches and into every spectator's chest. The crowd is shocked. He fought with those. "The prodigal son of the Zorak family," The king proudly exclaims, "the one who will lead Segovia into greatness."

files.title: (2)Foolish Old Man
files.description: Vivaan Kaushal
files.body: Vivaan Kaushal 3/25/26 1940 The fire pit crackles between them. Runox sits across from his father at the worn wooden table, eyes lowered. His mother stirs the pot at the hearth without turning, the curve of her back a quiet third presence in the hut. "These animals . . . they don't take me seriously, father. I train the same way as them — THE SAME exact way. Why can I not tame a Tarkan? The worst part is seeing all the other men tame theirs while I get left behind. I am behind, and the worst part is — I frankly don't care to tame a Tarkan. I am nothing in this society. A body with no use for itself," the despondent man says, finally lifting his gaze into the eyes of his father — predator's eyes, the eyes of a hunter. "WHAT DO YOU EXPECT, BOY! You have been given the blessing of the Luxian body and still cannot match your peers. On top of that, you DON'T CARE?! What will you do with your life, Runox?" his father groans, voice raspy and low. His hand rests flat on the table. The wood beneath his palm creaks — just once. "I DON'T CARE BECAUSE I DON'T WANT TO FALL INTO THIS LOOP THAT ALL OF YOU FALL INTO! Is this not a boring way to live? Do you not find this all meaningless? There is an entire world out there and we, as an empire, sit cradled in our little island. WHY DO WE EVEN TAME THE TARKAN IF WE DON'T FLY OUT?! Virethorian life is SUFFOCATING." The mother's spoon pauses in the pot. Just for a moment. Then it stirs on. Runox swallows the unspoken truth — that he has a natural edge over the rest of the empire, yet he cannot climb the same as them. "It is YOU who will suffocate yourself, boy, in your inability to act. You will DROWN in inaction. You have the potential to be the most ruthless soldier in this empire with that gifted body. You simply do not use it, and that is of your own choosing. And why is that, you say?" "It's because I do not care to, father. Why must I?" "SO then — what do you care about?" His father focuses his pupils on Runox's. Runox's face drains of life. He grumbles, "I want to annihilate the cult of All Father in The Luxian Empire." Runox has thought of leaving before. He is burdened, however, by the fact that these people raised him. He feels he owes them. "Childish FANTASIES. You cannot even beat your peers or tame a Tarkan — what makes you think YOU ARE SURVIVING ONE SECOND IN THE LUXIAN EMPIRE?! YOU have not even discovered your Power Core." His father leans his weight on the table. The wood groans. The legs sink an inch into the swamp wood floor. He does not seem to notice. The fire pops. "Boy . . . the truth is, I have no will to exert on you. I just want to see you become ruthless. I want you to be so free you can move the Earth." Runox hesitates. He is conflicted. In an immature attempt to stay defensive, he exclaims, "I deserve to see my homeland!" "We will not be taking you to the Hell Above — The Luxian Empire," his father closes the conversation. "You . . . are hopeless, boy. Leave my sight." Runox stands. He glances at his mother. She does not turn from the pot, but her hand has gone still. He lowers his eyes again and walks out. --- Runox steps into the wet Virethorian night, a boiling conflict he has never touched before churning in his chest. The air hangs thick and green-tinged, heavy with the Plagued Zone's damp; moss drips from the swamp wood overhead, and the dark canopy swallows what little sky there is. Dawn approaches. The Virethorian Guards trickle out for their defense shifts — fewer than usual. A garrison was sent into the deep swamp last night to chase a Luxian probe, and the Hangar has been left short. He stops beneath a marsh-rotted, dilapidated ancient tree near the swamp he fell into when the Luxians cast him out. A seed plants itself in his head. He takes a peek at the Hangar. *I can do both. I can pursue my will and satisfy my mother and father. I just need to take out the cult of All Father.* Runox walks to the Tarkan Hangar gates with a cold gaze. He is a whisper in the night, and each step exudes relentless power. The Virethorian Guards turn their eyes to the approaching terror. They ready their spears; their thorn-spiked armor and helmets bristle, defying any force. Runox does not slow. One guard fixes him with the gaze of death. He is not respected in this empire as a Luxian. The guard will pierce right through him given even little justification. --- The first guard thrusts his spear at Runox's head, unleashing a barbaric cry. Runox pivots to the left while grabbing the shaft with his left hand. He yanks — closing the distance in a single, brutal pull — and drives every ounce of his weight into a right cross through the gaps in the thorned armor. His fist crunches into the guard's nose. The helmet cracks. Runox's knuckles split open against the thorns. The guard collapses into the wet swamp wood underfoot. The second guard lunges. Runox glances down at his hand — The blood is not running. It has hardened. Dark red, glassy, crusted around his knuckles like a second skin. He stares at it for half a heartbeat. *What — ?* The second guard tackles him to the ground. Thorns sink into his chest, his shoulders, his ribs. Runox braces the fall with his right arm — The hardened blood cracks. A devastating explosion erupts around his hand. The blast rolls harmlessly across his own skin — somehow — and snaps his elbow upward like a piston, launching into the guard's face at an insanely fast speed. The skull caves in. Wet matter sprays the swamp wood walls. Somewhere deeper in the Hangar, a caged Tarkan snorts awake. Another roars in answer. The smell of dung and damp feathers thickens the air. Lanterns sway on their iron hooks. The third guard — the one with the horn — flinches at the blast and looks down at the body. "WHAT THE FUCK?! WHERE DID HE GO?!" Runox is gone. The guard raises the horn again. Faster this time. Runox swipes at the horn from behind and it falls. By now the neighboring villages are alerted; lanterns flicker awake in the dark. The guard and Runox engage in hand-to-hand combat. Runox throws a right cross — parried. A left hook — slipped. They trade blows in tight quarters, each strike echoing off the swamp wood walls. The caged Tarkans pace and snarl behind them. Runox dashes in and slams the side of his body against the guard, pinning him to the wall. He follows with a flurry of chops — knife edge, elbow, knife edge, elbow. The guard finds an opening, grabs Runox's neck fast, and slams him to the ground. Runox squeezes his arm. The guard grins, all teeth, and squeezes harder, sinking the thorns into Runox's neck. Then Runox remembers. He sees it — more hardened blood, crusted on the guard's hand from the choking. He smashes it with all his might. The hand explodes. Blood and bone gush out as the guard lets out a painful cry. Runox gets up hastily and sweeps the guard's leg. As the guard falls, Runox drives the man's head into the ground with the full force of the descent. A sickening crack. He needs to be as quick as possible. He punches the Hangar lock. The hardened blood cracks once again — a localized explosion — and the lock blows clean off. "This is where it works." Runox is filled with unwavering determination. --- He locates a Tarkan in the nearest cage. The beast is massive — saddle-broken but not friendly. It eyes him sidelong with one wet, intelligent eye, snorts a steaming breath into the cold damp, and bares its teeth. Runox steps closer. The Tarkan jerks against its tether. He places his bloodied hand against its flank and holds it there. The beast stills. They understand each other in the way prey understands fellow prey: tonight, both of them need to leave. He quickly straps on a set of high-grade Tarkan Jets, along with a breathing mask. Runox sloppily connects the metallic joints and screws. Despite his inexperience, he Frankensteins the gear on, ready for launch. Runox hesitates. He thinks of his mother — her hand going still over the pot, the unspoken goodbye in her quiet back. He reminds himself that this is merely a means to prove his natural gift was not given to him in vain — and that he will return. Runox guides the Tarkan outside and is met with a horde of angry villagers. He clicks on the Tarkan Jets and lets the Tarkan completely loose. The Tarkan roars and follows the thrust of the jet, launching off the land immediately. Runox does his best to keep the Tarkan on track — it is so much easier to handle a Tarkan with all this gear. "Why do they make us tame Tarkans without anything when we live in an era of this technology? With this gear, there is no need to tame a Tarkan by hand," Runox relishes in his achievement. --- The air pulls Runox's skin back as he continues to soar. Suddenly, flying spears emerge from below — the Virethorian guards are trying to take him down. Runox steers to the left, then to the right. The Tarkan's wings flap. He pulls up and steers to the left again. He cranks the engine — the whirring of the thruster builds, louder, hotter. He can feel the fire. The Tarkan puffs, the mechanical whirring of the breathing mask activating with each breath. The sky is filled with mechanical whirring, spearheads, and the adrenaline-filled breathing of Runox himself. The Tarkan continues to fly up and out of the island. The Tarkan squeals. A spearhead has pierced its left wing. It bucks under him. Runox grips the saddle handle tighter and feels — for the first time — the beast's pulse beneath his palm. It is afraid. Suddenly, Runox hears electricity mixed with a heavy fire. The left Tarkan Jet is pierced and down. Runox cranks the engine up even more to get out. The Tarkan flaps its wings in panic. The two are going so fast that Runox can barely see, even with his strong Luxian skin. His face is being utterly peeled and the wind cuts through. The Tarkan puffs and puffs. No mechanical whirring. Runox's eyes widen — the breathing mask has fallen off. "FUCK FUCK FUCK, I FUCKED UP PUTTING THE STRAP O——" A freshness so great washes over Runox he almost faints. The air is cool. So gentle. The stuffiness — gone. The damp green weight that has lived in his lungs for nineteen years — gone. He can see clearer than he ever has. *This is what it's like to fly weightless,* he thinks. It feels like finally entering the cold air after being trapped in a sauna for months. *This is what it feels like to SEE. To BREATHE. To LIVE.* Runox has exited the Plagued Zone. Runox looks down. "The green smog — it's BELOW ME!" He is in utter awe. He relishes in the experience. *Now then — I will stop at a nearby island and find a means to the Luxian Empire from there. It's so annoying how we have no maps in The Virethorian Empire. I have no idea where the Luxian Empire is. I could benefit from talking to someo——* "Wait a second — why is it getting hotter and hotter?" The burning sensation builds. Runox smells fuel in the air. The Tarkan is on fire. Runox cranked the engine too far. It begins to squeal and vigorously flap its wings. The Tarkan begins to fall — its lungs cannot hold weight without the plagued air to fill them. "NOT LIKE THIS, I'LL GET TO AN ISLAND!" Runox cranks the engine to the max. The Tarkan continues to soar. A lifeless ragdoll blasting through the air. A jet engine strapped to a carcass. The Tarkan continues to burn. The smell of burnt flesh fills the air, and the sound of cracking bone fills Runox's ears. The thrust shakes the very air around him. Runox flies farther and farther from the Plagued Zone, higher and higher. He looks behind him — the Tarkan parts closest to the jet engine are pure bone. One third of the Tarkan is a skeleton now. He grips the saddle handle harder. *I'm sorry,* he thinks. As Runox braces for a huge fall back down, he looks up with one last spark of hope. A single island emerges from the haziness of the sky. He smears his blood across the Tarkan's hide and watches it harden. He drops into a squatting position, one hand locked on the saddle handle. With all his might, he punches the hardened blood, jumping at the same time. The blast sends him soaring upward, and the Tarkan explodes into gory chunks below. Runox's hand catches the edge of the cliff. The hardened blood on his palm scrapes against rock and peels back. His knuckles split. His shoulder screams as his full weight tears against the joint. He hauls himself up, one ragged inch at a time, until he rolls onto solid stone. He lies there. Breathing. The island reveals itself. Beyond a low ridge, lanterns burn through a haze of smoke. Music drifts toward him — strings, a horn, voices in tongues he does not know. The clink of glass. The grind of cart wheels. A faraway shout, then laughter. Somewhere, a bell rings to mark an arrival. Runox cracks a bloody smile through bruised lips. *Foolish old man.* "I've done it!"

files.body: Vivaan Kaushal 7/6/25 1940 Chariot Backstory Chariot's skin begins to tingle and burn. Not in a bad way though. Rather, in the way one's chilled hands tingle when held too close to a fireplace. He enters his warm cabin after a long day of playing outside, relieved as the rush of heat brings his body back to normal temperature. It is one of the colder days in Nivora. "Mommy! Mommy! The Glacier Force — they're back, they're right there!” He grabs her sleeve, teeth knocking together. "Aren't they the coolest thing you've ever seen?" His mother's eyes widen as the photon of fear enters her pupils. Ten-year-old Chariot looks up to the Glacier Force, they are his heroes. To his mother, they are corpses still walking. She grabs her coat. "They must be coming in from their first reconnaissance mission, let's go see daddy!" --- The cold bites Chariot and his mother's cheeks as they leave their cabin. Chariot holds his mother's hand, struggling to keep up as he treks through the rough snow. Each step comes with a satisfying crunching sound. A couple of minutes of walking and they reach the crowd at the village entrance. Villagers line the road on both sides, leaving a narrow path for the returning soldiers. Some faces cling to hope, some sharpen with rage, and some are devoid of emotion. Some wait for loved ones, some for interviews, some for no reason at all. The Glacier Force is slowly revealed through the snowy fog. The soldiers pass through the entrance gate slowly, marching in perfect synchronization. As always, there is not an ounce of emotion on their faces. They look blank and devoid of any soul, almost… lifeless. Corpses are carried in dark brown, wooden carriages. Snow coats everyone, icicles hang from beards, and eyes are filled with anger, anguish, and hopelessness. Chunks of flesh are missing from people's bodies. A man, his cheek missing from what appears to be a giant bite, talks to himself in his carriage. His teeth and gums move up and down through the hole in his cheek as he recites what seems to be a prayer. He looks like he's going insane, crammed in a carriage, surrounded by others just like him, teetering on psychosis. There is not enough space in the carriages. Soldiers with lost arms or other chunks of their bodies continue to march forward in spite of their missing limbs. Not everyone gets the luxury of bleeding out in a wooden box. "You people are USELESS. All you do is go out and let more men DIE. What value did we derive from this reconnaissance, TELL ME," a villager shouts out. "Another bloody shit fest," says a fat-bellied, bearded man with what appears to be sauce stains on his shirt. The chief doesn't even glance at him. Two soldiers in the back collapse. Three more spit huge amounts of blood—one at the front of the line, his buddy next to him, and another in a carriage. The blood colors the snow red and drips from their chins. There is blood everywhere, on everyone. Chariot's mother closes her son's eyes as a carriage comes through with a barely-alive man. His intestines are littered all over the carriage and a slimy, pink tube hangs out of his belly from what appears to be a giant scratch mark. "What are THESE MEN DYING FOR!!!" "WHERE IS MY LOVE? WHERE IS HE? BRIGARD, ARE YOU THERE?" "IS THIS WHERE MY TAXES ARE GOING? TO YOU WORTHLESS LOT?! YOU ARE ALL USELESS FIGHTERS!" Tears roll off soldiers, villagers, and kids. Those same tears freeze in midair, turning into tiny cannonballs that crash onto the red, bloodshot snow beneath. The soldiers continue marching forward; no glances, no emotions, only their lifeless pupils. This is not new for them; these soldiers risk their lives every week on these reconnaissance missions. Why? The Snowbiter Hunt. Every year, these highly intelligent, giant, saber-toothed, albino snow beasts, known as Snowbiters, prepare their pack for a hunt. The villagers of Nivora are the prey. It is unknown when in the year the Snowbiters will strike. The job of the Glacier Force is to find out and alert the town and militia. They go out as a group into Snowbiter territory and check if the pack is out of hibernation. There are always Snowbiters guarding the hibernation spots as a defense, and the Glacier Force has to deal with that every time. They come back with significant casualties. The people are THE PREY. They will do anything in their power to survive. "DADDY!" Chariot finds his father in the squadron of troops—soulless as usual, fists clenched, obvious sorrow written on his face. Chariot's mother stops him from running to his father. "Good, he is safe. Let's head home and meet him tonight in time for dinner. They need to report the status to the chairmen." The only thing in Chariot's mind is how cool these men are. Risking their lives to keep the town alert. Brave soldiers. Skilled warriors. Fearless. Suddenly, a quivering, scrawny villager stops the chief in his tracks. "H-H-HEY, my daughter is a h-h-huge fan of yours and I was wondering if you could give me an auto-aut-autograph for her." The chief stands tall, towering over the villager. He peers down at him with his one remaining eye, showing no signs of emotion or acknowledgment. A man in the back of the troop screams in anguish as blood spurts out of his thigh. Lost-limbed soldiers pant from exhaustion. The chief has said a thousand words to this villager without a single vibration from his voice box. He shoves the villager to the side, not lightly, and continues the march. "What asshats. These villagers don't appreciate or understand what these soldiers really do for us. Most of these people have never seen a Snowbiter. Ungrateful wretches. Let's go home, Chariot." The two depart back to their cabin, leaving behind the still-yelling, complaining and anguished crowd. --- Many hours pass and Chariot's father still hasn't returned home. "Chariot, listen to me. When you are older, I do not want you to join the Glacier Force—it is a death sentence. Focus on math; you love math, don’t you? I used to teach numbers, before I came here, before all of this. You have a sharper mind than I ever did. You should work on becoming a great mathematician and leave Nivora when you can to show the world what you can do. It is not safe here regardless," Chariot's mother says. "I want to beat those Snowbiters to a pulp. I know I can do it. I'll be just like daddy," Chariot passionately says. Something passes behind Chariot's eyes—just for a flicker, something that is not a child's anger. His mother sees it. She has seen it before. Chariot's mother grabs his arms tightly. "YOU LISTEN TO ME—DO NOT! YOU WILL UNDERSTAND WHEN YOU'RE OLDER! YOU HAVE TO LISTEN TO ME, CHARIOT, PLEASE, BABY, PLEASE!" She abruptly breaks into tears as she relinquishes her grip on his arms. Just as Chariot goes to comfort her, a town announcement plays on the tall speakers. "ATTENTION ALL CITIZENS, A SNOWBITER RAID IS IMMINENT. BARRICADE YOUR HOUSES. THE MILITARY WILL BE OUT SHORTLY. ENFORCE PROPER PROTOCOL. GRAB WEAPONS AND HIDE UNDERGROUND. I REPEAT, A SNOWBITER RAID IS IMMINENT! " Silence fills the room abruptly. Many of the military men have power core abilities, though none very strong. The sound of thousands of boots running and crunching through the snow echoes throughout the town. Chariot and his mother have gone through this protocol lots of times. They know their father's life is at risk and they know what to do to stay secure. Chariot and his mother rush to barricade the walls as much as possible—planks, tables, and reinforced metal. Chariot's mother feels a chill down her spine. *Why is it so abrupt? Did the Glacier Force miss something? This can't be fucking happening.* "THEY ARE HERE EARLY!" A soldier outside yells in agony as a squelching snap ends his life. The crunching of bones and squishing fills the air. The varied sounds of power core abilities fill the village. The sounds of screaming and painful yells. The sounds of fire from imported Scorch Slime grenades. The sounds of arrows flying and icicle guns. All these sounds, all at once. It's chaos. P A N I C ensues Loud banging erupts on the walls and doors of Chariot and his mother's cabin. "LET USSS INNN LET USSS INN PLEA–" A squelching, crunching sound cuts off the pleading speech. Many of these men are facing a Snowbiter for the first time. They are completely paralyzed by fear. It is not uncommon for soldiers to hide, freeze, panic or try to escape. A man crouched behind three wine barrels near the barracks watches a Snowbiter peel a soldier open at the ribs—the soldier still alive, still screaming through it, his lungs working as the beast feeds. The man has seen what these creatures do to those caught alive. He would rather not find out for himself. He sticks his gun in his mouth and fires, painting the snow with his brains. There are, however, some brave soldiers who put up a solid fight, typically those with Power Core abilities. The Snowbiters charge into the town, seeping into the residential areas and devouring everyone. The beasts pour into Nivora like an avalanche of fangs and claws. This year, the hunt came abruptly; the town didn't have enough time to prepare. Chariot's mother continues covering him up as tears roll down her face. Screams, squeezing, cracking, squelching. An utter massacre happens outside as Chariot and his mother sit in fear within the confines of the small, homey wooden cabin. It is completely dark inside, save for the warm red light from the fireplace, and Chariot and his mother don't make a single sound. The security and isolation of the cabin is almost warm and reassuring, but at the same time a vulnerable feeling lingers throughout; it's chilling. The Snowbiters burst through the village with a force that makes walls crumble under the weight of their charge, their roars cutting through the blizzard like thunder. Even more soldiers rush to meet them, spears braced, but the Snowbiters tear through the lines with a speed that mocks human strength; armor bends like tin beneath their jaws, shields splinter with a single swipe of claws rimed in frost. Panic spreads faster than fire, and families flee into the snow, only to be dragged down screaming, choking on the snow, their cries muffled as the pack sinks its teeth into where they fall. Blood steams against the white ground, staining the village in broad strokes of red. More and more soldiers come knocking on the cabin. "Don't worry, Chariot, just be quiet okay? Daddy will kill them all," Chariot's mother attempts to comfort her son as she mentally crumbles and descends into madness. The cabin continues to sit buried in snowdrifts like a jewel of warmth in a frozen, barbaric wilderness, its log walls glowing gold under the firelight that leaks through frosted windows. The barricades make it feel even more secure. The two are untouchable and the warmth of the cabin hugs them. More sounds come from the door. This time it's an erratic scratching, wood audibly chipping off. That soldier must be in excruciating pain. A giant paw blasts through the door, sending wood flying through the house. The second paw enters. In the blink of an eye the entire wall is utterly demolished and a single Snowbiter menacingly lays its eyes upon Chariot and his mother. Its gaze is gut-wrenching. The white fur blows in the wind like dancing grass. So majestic yet so cruel. The grey lining of the fur is stained with blood. Human eyes, guts, and fat tissue are stuck in its teeth. It grunts and snarls as it closes in, faster and faster. The warmth in the cabin suddenly disappears as the merciless cold of Nivora rushes in. Chariot's mother glances at Chariot, seeing a sharp chip of wood lodged in his pupil. Blood drips out. His eyes weep crimson tears, dripping faster and faster. "GET AWAY FROM US!" Chariot's mother grabs her spear. Both Chariot and his mother brace. Chariot is too numb to even feel the pain of his pierced eye. He picks up his spear with nothing but pure hatred. He looks the Snowbiter in the eye. "Chariot, stay behind me NOW!" Chariot's mother shields him. Every step the Snowbiter takes shakes the cabin. Each step feels like it shakes the very fabric of reality for Chariot's mother. The Snowbiter lunges. Chariot's mother hurls the spear at the Snowbiter, and it snaps the weapon between its paws like a twig. One swipe is all it takes. Chariot thrusts his spear at the beast. A squelch sounds out. His spear pierces the Snowbiter's neck. Chariot looks up with a small flame of hope. All color fades from his pupils as he sees the utter horror that towers above him. The Snowbiter's massive fangs are sunk into his mother's neck. The beast crunches harder and her neck snaps with a cracking, squelching sound. The Snowbiter jerks up and rips her head right off. Chariot watches in agony as this unfolds, his spear flying off the Snowbiter. With one final crunch, his mother's head is devoured whole, one eyeball flying out and landing right on Chariot's foot. Chariot's entire stomach is filled to the brim with a sharp burning feeling and tears roll from his eyes, mixing with the blood coming from the gaping hole in his eye socket. His eyes sting, but not from the pain of the wood. Chariot rushes at the Snowbiter with bare fists, tears skewing his vision. The Snowbiter sinks its fearsome claws into Chariot's face, pinning him down to the floor. Its claws have just turned his other eye into meat stew, burrowing deep into the socket. Chariot screams in such agony it sends shivers through the whole village, cutting through all the commotion already happening. Chariot can no longer see anything. He keeps screaming and flailing. Darkness devours him as he desperately continues punching and slapping at the thick, meaty, furry arm pinning him. "W-W-WHY WON'T YOU JUST DIEEEEEE!" Then— A huge shake and thud rip through the house from nowhere. The crushing weight on Chariot's chest suddenly vanishes. Next comes an explosion. Not a normal explosion. The sound of ruffling and grappling, followed by a giant meat ball erupting. Hot, wet matter splatters across his face. The smell of dead Snowbiter fills the room and Chariot lies still, petrified. He cannot see it, but the Snowbiter has just been completely mangled, torn apart, its red guts splattered like paint across the walls. Chariot reaches blindly for his mother. His fingers find wet floor. He gropes further, palm dragging through warm matter that is not the meat of a Snowbiter. He feels something soft. He feels nothing where her head should be. Chariot stands up, seemingly unfazed. He sees nothing. He only feels the warm wet slick on his face that isn't his, and hears the silence where the Snowbiter's snarls used to be. --- Hiding soldiers look at the cabin entrance with curiosity. Out walks a tall, hulking figure: matte black from head to toe, no face, no features at all, just a black silhouette covered in matte-black armor reminiscent of a medieval knight. One couldn't even call it a man, more like an entity. This being has just single-handedly eviscerated a Snowbiter within the cabin with its bare hands. The "man" sprints at immense speed, rushing out of the cabin. It targets every Snowbiter it sees. It draws a rapier and jabs at one Snowbiter insanely fast, pushing the blade in and out three times a second, leaving thousands of gushing holes in the Snowbiter's torso. The Snowbiter collapses in agony. The "man" leans on his back leg, bracing for something. He pushes forward and dashes into a sprint with such immense power it cracks the ground behind him. He runs around the village, slashing every single Snowbiter in sight. Heads coming clean off, bodies being cut in half, brains being pierced. As the man gets farther from Chariot, his armor slowly comes off until he stands naked. He impales Snowbiters with his bare hands. He drives his knuckles right through the heads of more and more Snowbiters. He wrestles some, getting them in chokeholds, snapping their necks. Hours pass and, with the combined efforts of this "man" and the soldiers, the Snowbiters perish and the remaining ones retreat. Chariot's father runs to the cabin and is struck with complete terror as he looks at the mangled remains of his wife. A few meters behind the remains stands Chariot, completely emotionless, eyes gushing red. In front of him is a black void on the ground, sort of like a hole. "THE BLACK MAN, H-H-HE CAME FROM THE CABIN!" a quivering soldier whimpers. Could this portal be where the man came from? Is this… Chariot's Power Core Ability?
